pattern_id: Commit Vote Equivocation Causing Divergent Linearization
description:
A Byzantine node can create two equivocating blocks at the same (round, author) slot with identical ancestors but different commit_votes, then selectively broadcast them to different honest nodes. This causes honest nodes to make different commit decisions and produce divergent linearized sequences, violating safety even though they agree on the DAG structure up to the equivocation point.

The vulnerability manifests because:
1. The protocol allows blocks with the same (round, author) but different content (including commit_votes) to exist in different nodes' views
2. Commit votes influence which blocks get committed in the linearization process
3. When different honest nodes see different commit_votes from the Byzantine node, they make different commit decisions
4. This leads to divergent linearized sequences, breaking the fundamental safety property that all honest nodes must agree on the same sequence

The attack is particularly insidious because:
- The DAG structure appears valid to each honest node individually
- No single node can detect the equivocation without comparing notes with other nodes
- The divergence cascades to subsequent rounds as honest nodes build on different equivocating blocks
- Standard equivocation detection (same slot, different blocks) may not trigger if nodes don't share their views
trigger_condition:
1. Byzantine node is scheduled to propose at a round
2. Byzantine node creates two blocks at the same (round, author) with:
   - Identical ancestors
   - Different commit_votes (voting for different blocks to commit)
   - Same or different transactions
3. Byzantine node selectively broadcasts the equivocating blocks to different subsets of honest nodes
4. Honest nodes build subsequent rounds on top of their respective equivocating blocks
5. Commit logic is triggered (sufficient rounds accumulated)
6. Linearization produces different sequences for different honest nodes
